newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: UNION MINIERE RAISES STAKE IN DUTCH UNIT.
newsitem.headline: UNION MINIERE RAISES STAKE IN DUTCH UNIT.

text.p: Dutch metals firm Koninklijke Maastrichtsche Zinkwit-Maatschappij NV said on Wednesday it was now 98 percent owned by its Belgian parent Union Miniere International BV.

"Negotiations between Union Miniere and representatives of a number of minority shareholders have resulted in an agreement on the takeover of at least 25,000 ordinary shares in Koninklijke Maastrichtsche Zinkwit-Maatschappij," the company said.
It added the shares had been sold at 290 guilders each.
Previously Union Miniere owned a 93 percent interest.
Union Miniere offers an exit opportunity to the remaining shareholders to sell their stock at 290 guilders per share until the end of this year.

Maastrichtsche Zinkwit was listed on the Amsterdam Stock until 1989. The company was delisted when Union Miniere, already a majority stakeholder, made a bid for the remaining shares but not all shares were tendered.
